description: Doenjang Jjigae is a comforting and hearty Korean soybean paste stew, a staple in Korean households. It features a savory, umami-rich broth made with doenjang, simmered with an assortment of fresh vegetables, silky tofu, and sometimes meat or seafood. This versatile dish is deeply flavorful and perfect for any meal, offering a taste of authentic Korean home cooking.

instructions.title: Prepare Broth and Vegetables
instructions.text: If using anchovy broth, prepare it by simmering dried anchovies and kombu in water for 15-20 minutes, then strain. Otherwise, use plain water. Dice the tofu, zucchini, radish or potato, and slice the onion and mushrooms. Mince the garlic and slice the green onion and chili pepper.

instructions.title: Combine Doenjang and Broth
instructions.text: In a medium pot or dolsot (earthenware pot), add the doenjang and a small amount of the prepared broth. Stir well to dissolve the doenjang completely, forming a smooth paste. This prevents lumps in your stew.

instructions.title: Add Initial Vegetables and Broth
instructions.text: Pour in the remaining broth. Add the diced radish or potato and sliced onion to the pot. Bring the mixture to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce heat to medium. Simmer for about 10 minutes until the radish or potato starts to soften.

instructions.title: Introduce More Ingredients
instructions.text: Add the minced garlic, sliced zucchini, and mushrooms to the pot. If using, also add the gochugaru and sliced Cheongyang chili pepper for an extra kick. Stir gently to combine all ingredients.

instructions.title: Add Tofu and Simmer
instructions.text: Carefully add the diced tofu to the stew. Avoid stirring too vigorously to prevent breaking the tofu. Continue to simmer for another 5-7 minutes, allowing all the flavors to meld and the vegetables to cook through. The tofu should be heated thoroughly.

instructions.title: Final Touches and Serve
instructions.text: Taste and adjust seasoning if needed; you might add a pinch more doenjang or a dash of salt. Stir in the chopped green onions just before serving. For an extra layer of flavor, drizzle with a touch of sesame oil. Serve hot with a bowl of freshly cooked rice and various banchan (side dishes).

tips: For a richer flavor, use a homemade anchovy-kombu broth instead of plain water. The umami from the dried anchovies and kelp significantly deepens the stew's taste.
Doenjang quality varies greatly. Invest in a good quality, traditional Korean doenjang for the most authentic and robust flavor. Some brands are saltier than others, so adjust quantity to taste.
Doenjang Jjigae is best enjoyed immediately while hot. Serve it directly in the dolsot it was cooked in to keep it sizzling at the table, a classic Korean presentation.
